messages:
michelle_support: Heads up — AcmeCorp reports intermittent SSO failures since their IdP cert rotation ~10:00 UTC. A few users get a 401 / 'Assertion signature invalid: key not found'. Happening on our production connector only.

sam_eng: Can you paste the exact assertion error from the logs and the IdP metadata URL?

michelle_support: Log snippet: ```
ERROR auth.saml: SignatureValidationError: no matching key found for SignatureValue
RequestId: rq_9a2f...
Destination: https://redwood.example.com/sso/acs
```
IdP metadata: https://idp.acme.example/metadata.xml

sam_eng: Thanks. Can you download the metadata and show the <KeyDescriptor> ordering near the top? In past cases a rotated key was added as use="encryption" and pushed before signing keys, our parser historically picked the first KeyDescriptor which caused validation to try the wrong key.

michelle_support: Pulled the metadata and here is the relevant excerpt: ```xml
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acme.example">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="encryption">
      <KeyInfo>...new-key (SHA256)...</KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo>...old-key (RSA)...</KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```

javier_sre: Yep — that's the pattern. If metadata has encryption key first, our old metadata consumer sometimes picks the first KeyDescriptor as 'signing'. Quick workaround: ask IdP to mark the signing key explicit (use="signing") and/or move it before encryption in their metadata. Also we can add a temporary fallback on our side to prefer KeyDescriptor[@use='signing'] when present.

sam_eng: Agreed. Short-term: ask Acme to re-order or set use attributes correctly. Medium-term: we'll harden parser so it selects keys by use attribute instead of position and fall back to trying all keys. I can prepare a patch.

michelle_support: Customer asked for a concrete repro so they can send to IdP team. Any quick commands we can give them?

sam_eng: Yes. Ask them to run: 
```bash
curl -sSL https://idp.acme.example/metadata.xml | xmllint --format - | sed -n '1,120p'
```
Then check ordering of <KeyDescriptor> under <IDPSSODescriptor>. Or run this Python one-liner to find which KeyDescriptor is signing: 
```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
from lxml import etree
md=etree.parse('/dev/stdin')
for kd in md.xpath('//IDPSSODescriptor/KeyDescriptor'):
    print(kd.get('use'))
PY < metadata.xml
```
Share that output with us.

michelle_support: Forwarded to Acme. They confirmed they injected the new cert with use="encryption" and didn't reorder. They can change it but it'll be a few hours. Any temporary config on our side to avoid user impact?

javier_sre: We can flip a config on the connector to prefer KeyDescriptor use='signing' — low-risk and reversible. I'll open a small internal PR and stage it on staging. If tests pass we can deploy to production as a safety net. :white_check_mark:

alyssa_pm: Looping in account team so they know this will affect some users during rotation window. Alyssa — please ping Acme with ETA and workaround steps.

idp-bot: metadata-refresh: fetched https://idp.acme.example/metadata.xml at 2025-03-17T10:02:12Z, sha256=3f7a...

michelle_support: Thanks — I'll tell Acme their immediate action is to mark the signing key with use=\"signing\" or reorder, and we'll proceed with the connector fix if they can't update quickly. Keep me posted on the PR and staging results.

sam_eng: PR #4289 opened (saml: prefer explicit signing KeyDescriptor). I'll link results here once CI + staging pass.

michelle_support: Appreciate it — moving to high priority until rotation window closes.
